# /wall/[id]/prompt-packs/[packId]

Step 2 of the pack picker: one pack's prompts, multi-select up to a cap,
then add the selection to the wall. It closes the loop the catalog screen
opens, and its write is the point of the whole two-step flow.

## At a glance

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Route | `/wall/[id]/prompt-packs/[packId]` |
| Router file | `app/wall/[id]/prompt-packs/[packId].tsx` |
| Flows | F7 Wall creation and administration |
| Position in flow | step 2 of 2, `/wall/[id]/prompt-packs` -> here -> `/family` |
| Data calls | one read (`getPromptPack`), one write (`injectWallPrompts`) |
| Shared surface | `ScreenHeader` |

Cited to hs2studio/scribl-app at `c1b3c2d` on `main`, clean tree.

## Features

| Feature | Where it lives |
|---------|----------------|
| View one pack's full prompt list | `app/wall/[id]/prompt-packs/[packId].tsx:78-103` |
| Select prompts, up to `MAX_INJECT_PROMPTS` (5) | `app/wall/[id]/prompt-packs/[packId].tsx:34-44`, cap defined `src/stores/useWallPromptsStore.ts:9` |
| Add the selected prompts to the wall | `app/wall/[id]/prompt-packs/[packId].tsx:46-52`, `111-121` |
| Retry the pack-detail load on failure | `app/wall/[id]/prompt-packs/[packId].tsx:67-75` |

`MAX_INJECT_PROMPTS` is 5, and the screen's own comment says the server caps
it, not this UI: "the number is ours" refers to interpreting Eric's spoken
"a couple" as this specific limit, not to the enforcement, which happens
server-side (`app/wall/[id]/prompt-packs/[packId].tsx:16-20`). Selecting a
sixth prompt is a silent no-op client-side (`:39`), which is a UX gap: there
is no message telling the person why the tap did nothing.

## Data calls

This is the write that the two-screen picker exists for. Selecting a pack on
the catalog screen is read-only browsing; choosing prompts here and
submitting is the real, server-persisted action.

| Client method | Endpoint | Handler |
|---------------|----------|---------|
| `getPromptPack(packId)` | `GET /prompt-packs/:packId` | `backend/lambda/handlers/prompt-pack-detail.ts` |
| `injectWallPrompts(channelId, packId, promptIds)` | `POST /walls/:channelId/prompts` | `backend/lambda/handlers/wall-prompts-create.ts` |

Both methods are on `src/data/http.ts` (`getPromptPack:416-421`,
`injectWallPrompts:449-464`). The screen calls the read through
`usePromptPacksStore.loadDetail(packId)` (`app/wall/[id]/prompt-packs/[packId].tsx:24`,
`30-32`) and the write through `useWallPromptsStore.inject()`
(`:25`, `46-52`). A 403 (not the creator) or 400 (bad pack or prompt id, or
over the cap) surfaces as `injectError` text on the screen rather than a
silent failure, per the screen's own doc comment (`:16-20`) and the
rendered error at `:106-110`.

## State in, state out

**Reads on entry.** The route's `id` and `packId` params
(`app/wall/[id]/prompt-packs/[packId].tsx:23`); the pack detail, loaded on
mount keyed on `packId` (`:30-32`).

**Writes on mount.** None beyond the detail fetch.

**Writes on exit.** On a successful inject: the chosen prompts are written
to the wall on the server, and the screen replaces to `/family` with the
wall in context (`:49-51`). `router.replace`, not `push` -- this screen is
not meant to be backed into once the add succeeds.

## Notes for planning

Authored here, not read out of the app.

### The catalog is browsing, this screen is the write

Of the two screens, only this one changes anything. A person can open every
pack in the catalog and back out with nothing persisted; the wall's prompts
change only when a selection here is submitted. Worth stating plainly for
planning, since the two screens look like one flow but carry very different
risk: one is free to explore, one is not.

### Hitting the cap is silent

Tapping a sixth prompt while five are already selected does nothing
(`:39`), no toast, no shake, no disabled-row styling change visible in the
tile. A person who does not notice the "0/5 selected" counter has no signal
that their tap was ignored. Small, but it is the kind of thing that reads as
a bug in a demo.

### The label "a couple" versus the number 5 is worth surfacing once, not per-screen

The screen's own comment flags that the cap of 5 is a product decision
standing in for a vaguer verbal instruction ("a couple"). That is exactly
the kind of number a planning session should either ratify or change once,
rather than rediscovering from a code comment later.
